To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genome of the hyperthermostable microbe Pyrococcus furiosisus contains at least 1,500 open reading frames (orfs) and that there are at least 100 orfs that have been misannotated in the two major public databases (NCBI and TIGR).
the number and sizes (and, therefore, the identities) of many ORFs in microbial genomes have been inaccurately predicted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the archaeal and bacterial cell membranes interact with the environment, and how these interactions influence the cell's ability to grow and divide.
the definition of genes in microbial genomes.
the annotation of genes in the genome of the hyperthermostable, anaerobic, marine archaebacterium Pyrococcus furiosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number and sizes, as well as the identities, of ORFs in microbial genomes are not yet known with any accuracy.
there are approximately 2,100 genes in the genome of P. furiusus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the original annotation of the P. furious genome was correct in most instances, but that the genome contains a significant number of previously unannotated genes.
the P. furiosus genome contains 2,082 ORFs.
the number of ORFs in the original annotation was overestimated by approximately 10%, and that the sizes of the ORFs were overestimated in approximately 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current genome annotations for all microorganisms need to be reexamined and reevaluated.
the genome sequence of P. furio-sus is not complete, and the number of ORFs in this genome is likely to be greater than 2,000.
there are a large number of ORFs that were not annotated in the original genome annotation and that the two databases (TIGR and NC-BI) have different opinions about what the genome actually contains.
